analysis:
The supplied units are head-side excerpts (lines 1-797) of docs/architecture/inference.md, a documentation-only change. The changed ranges (head 2071-2114 and 2193-2198) are about Flint reasoning withholding and fall outside the displayed text, so I examined only the surrounding Nemotron Super and GLM5Next prose and the patch excerpt, which is truncated. No code, configuration or control changes are visible in the supplied evidence.

The Flint patch excerpt describes withheld reasoning via NativeToolStreamRouter, accepted and ignored reasoning controls, refusal of malformed values, preserve_thinking and media, and filtered logprobs. The documented behavior is that withheld reasoning is hidden from chat completions, Responses and the coordinator relay. The response hash covers only emitted output, and withheld tokens are still counted in usage. This text appears to be consistent with the provider-to-coordinator contract. It cannot be verified against the source because no Swift implementation is supplied. It does not obviously touch T-041 (prefix cache, TTFT oracle) or its at-rest posture. Whether FlintReasoningLogprobsFilter actually matches the documented behavior, and whether billing and reasoning_tokens accounting are correct, would need source review of FlintRequestPolicy, NativeToolStreamRouter and FlintReasoningLogprobsFilter.

The Nemotron sections in the displayed text describe prefix-cache scope partitioning by authenticated tenant scope, with no cache scope meaning cold and never publishing. They also describe no cache receipts. These are descriptive and consistent with the T-041 scoping mitigations. I identified no concrete security regression. The remaining uncertainty is that the doc claims are unverified against the code, which is outside this batch and not evidence of a flaw.
